brief: Build a 3D-printing station from the starter base. At the back, five columns three storeys tall stand in a row along q at r 0 (the starter at q 0, then q 2, 4, 6 and 8), with the cells between them left empty; each column carries rod sockets on its top storey facing the gaps, a spool axle spans each gap, and a 1 kg filament spool hangs on each of the four axles. Each column is topped with a shallow three-compartment bin of M3 screws and nuts. In front, toward the viewer at r 1, a one-storey counter runs from q 0 to q 7 and ties the columns together: covers on q 0 to 3 make the work surface, with a task lamp on the left end, a pencil cup, a hex driver set standing and a hex key set; shallow divided bins on q 4 and q 5 hold screws and nuts; half bases on q 6 and q 7 carry two drawers pulled open toward the viewer, for nozzles, hex keys and tweezers. Cap the open faces, bolt the joints, and leave the meshes clear.

M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
